description: Six image-acquisition records: polarized salt crystals, NIH fluorescence microscopy, unicellular Paramecium, osteology, precision hand work, and iris anatomy. License and scientific encoding caveats retained.

images.title: Salt crystals in polarized light
images.summary: Crystalline salt specimens photographed through a polarized-light microscope by Juan Carlos Fonseca Mata in Mexico in 2020. Different optical properties produce vivid interference colors.
images.alt: Small salt crystals appearing iridescent green, blue and orange against a pale peach microscope field.
images.caption: Real polarized-light micrograph of crystalline salts. The vivid optical colors come from specimen-light interactions under polarization, not the natural naked-eye colors of table salt.
images.credit: Juan Carlos Fonseca Mata / Universidad de Guanajuato
images.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 International. © Juan Carlos Fonseca Mata. https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ . This resized JPEG derivative is shared under CC BY-SA 4.0; modification disclosed.
images.processing: Original observational image converted to a development JPEG, maximum edge 1800 px, quality 87, source image URL and photographer retained. No AI generation.

images.title: Fluorescent microscopy of human HeLa cells
images.summary: A multiphoton fluorescence micrograph from the US National Institutes of Health reveals the actin cytoskeleton, microtubules and nuclei in cultured HeLa cells.
images.alt: Interlocking cells with bright cyan microtubule networks, red actin filaments and blue-violet nuclei on black.
images.caption: Human-derived HeLa cells, named after Henrietta Lacks, imaged in culture. Red staining marks actin, cyan marks microtubules and blue marks nuclei. These are fluorescence label colors.
images.credit: US National Institutes of Health / National Center for Microscopy and Imaging Research
images.rights: US federal government official work, public domain in the United States per Wikimedia Commons file documentation; review partner contribution rights separately.
images.processing: Original observational image converted to a development JPEG, maximum edge 1800 px, quality 87, source image URL and photographer retained. No AI generation. NIH multiphoton microscopy false-color channels preserved.

images.title: A unicellular ciliate with green algal symbionts
images.summary: A light-microscope photograph at a stated 400× magnification shows Paramecium bursaria, a free-living aquatic ciliate that commonly contains green algal cells inside its body.
images.alt: Single oblong translucent ciliate surrounded by fine cilia, containing many small green algal symbionts.
images.caption: Paramecium bursaria, a single-celled eukaryote photographed with light microscopy. Internal green algal symbionts share space within this ciliate.
images.credit: Picturepest (Flickr), CC BY 2.0; license reviewed by FlickreviewR in 2015
images.rights: CC BY 2.0 Generic (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/). Photograph © Picturepest; credited and linked, with resizing declared.
images.processing: Original observational image converted to a development JPEG, maximum edge 1800 px, quality 87, source image URL and photographer retained. No AI generation.

images.title: An articulated human skeleton
images.summary: An articulated human skeleton on exhibit at the Museum of Osteology in Oklahoma City, photographed in March 2010, demonstrates how bones form a structural framework.
images.alt: Pale beige articulated human skull, rib cage, spine, pelvis, arms and upper legs on a dark gray background.
images.caption: Exhibit skeleton photographed in Oklahoma City. Major features visible include skull, clavicles, ribs, vertebrae, pelvis and limb bones; this is a prepared display specimen.
images.rights: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, as recorded on the linked Commons file page. Photographer credited for provenance.
images.processing: Original observational image converted to a development JPEG, maximum edge 1800 px, quality 87, source image URL and photographer retained. No AI generation.

images.title: Human hands shape a rotating clay vessel
images.summary: Hands control and shape wet clay on a spinning potter's wheel in Springdale, Arkansas, photographed by Jared Sluyter in March 2017.
images.alt: Close view from above of two clay-covered human hands shaping the opening of a spinning pottery vessel.
images.caption: The coordinated movement of fingers and thumbs lets people manipulate material precisely. This photograph shows pottery production using a rotating wheel.
images.rights: CC0 1.0 dedication by photographer on Unsplash before June 5, 2017 license change; Wikimedia Commons original record documents historic CC0 publication.
images.processing: Original observational image converted to a development JPEG, maximum edge 1800 px, quality 87, source image URL and photographer retained. No AI generation.

images.title: A human iris and pupil
images.summary: An intimate close-up photograph of a person's brown iris, black pupil, white sclera and surrounding eyelids and eyelashes. These visible structures participate in vision.
images.alt: Extreme close-up of a brown human iris surrounding a black round pupil, with reflection on the eye and eyelashes visible.
images.caption: The iris regulates how much light reaches the lens by changing the pupil's diameter. Eye coloration and anatomy vary among individuals; this is one example.
images.rights: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, as recorded on the linked Commons file page. Photographer credited for provenance.
